steps.stage: Evidence law: Former statements of witness may be proved to corroborate later testimony as to same fact
steps.text: This section allows a witness's own earlier statement, relating to the same fact, to be proved as corroboration of his testimony where it was made at or about the time the fact took place, or before an authority legally competent to investigate the fact. It does not by itself make statements recorded by the police during investigation usable as corroboration: such statements are governed by the bar in BNSS section 181 (CrPC section 162), under which such a statement, where the witness is called for the prosecution, may be used by the accused, and by the prosecution only with the permission of the Court, to contradict the maker in the manner provided by BSA 148, any part so used being available in re-examination only to explain a matter raised in cross-examination, but not to corroborate, save for the statements taken outside that bar by BNSS section 181(2) (CrPC section 162(2)), namely a dying declaration admissible under BSA 26(a) and a statement admissible under the proviso to BSA 23(2). That bar bites only on a statement made to a police officer in the course of an investigation. A statement made before the investigation begins is not caught by it, and the first information report itself, recorded by the officer in charge of the police station, who is an authority legally competent to investigate the fact, may be proved under this section to corroborate the informant when he gives evidence, as well as used to contradict him under BSA 148; the FIR should therefore be recorded and timed with that use in view. The first limb imposes no condition on the person to whom the former statement was made, and a statement made to a private person is not touched by the BNSS section 181 bar, which reaches only statements made to a police officer in the course of an investigation. A witness's contemporaneous account to whoever he first spoke to, such as the victim's first disclosure to a family member, a neighbour or a friend, may therefore be proved under this section to corroborate him, provided it was made at or about the time when the fact took place. The IO should record who the witness first spoke to, when, and in what terms, and examine that person. The IO should record every statement promptly and enter the date and time of recording, which the investigation record requires in any event (statements under BNSS section 180, and the day-by-day case diary under BNSS section 192); nearness in time to the fact matters under this section only for a former statement outside the BNSS section 181 bar, and does not bring a statement recorded by the police during investigation within this section. Where a statement is recorded by an authority other than the police in the course of investigation, for example a Magistrate recording under BNSS section 183 (CrPC section 164), the IO should place on record that authority's competence and the circumstances of recording, which is what the second limb turns on.

bsa_refs.title: Former statements of witness may be proved to corroborate later testimony as to same fact
bsa_refs.summary: Former statements of witness may be proved to corroborate later testimony as to same fact. The section permits a witness's own earlier statement to be proved for the limited purpose of corroborating his later testimony. The former statement must have been made by that same witness and must relate to the same fact. It qualifies for proof on either of two footings: that it was made at or about the time when the fact took place, or that it was made before any authority legally competent to investigate the fact. The provision is a single sentence with no sub-sections, explanation or illustrations. It is permissive: the statement 'may be proved'. It does not direct that a former statement shall be treated as corroboration, nor does it fix what weight the Court is to give it, and it says nothing about the admissibility of any statement under any other law.
key_requirements: In order to corroborate the testimony of a witness, a former statement made by that witness may be proved; the section permits proof and does not direct that the statement shall be treated as corroboration.
The former statement must be one made by that same witness relating to the same fact, and made at or about the time when the fact took place.
Alternatively, the former statement may be proved if it was made before any authority legally competent to investigate the fact.
bsa_refs.investigation_relevance: This section allows a witness's own earlier statement, relating to the same fact, to be proved as corroboration of his testimony where it was made at or about the time the fact took place, or before an authority legally competent to investigate the fact. The second limb carries no timing condition of its own; it turns instead on the statement having been made before an authority legally competent to investigate the fact.
